sections.name: Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.

items.text: Hybrid models · What a buyer reads first
Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.
Two businesses in one transaction. The split decides whether you are priced as software or as a services business with a product.
Revenue, cost of revenue and gross margin for each, by month. A buyer builds the split if you have not, and prices the whole company on the result.

Practitioners put the threshold that changes how you are priced somewhere between 15 and 35 percent of revenue. Nobody publishes realized multiples by share. A buyer decides case by case, from your split.
One-time, or part of the subscription
Implementation fees bundled into the subscription inflate ARR. Billed apart, they are services. A buyer restates them to the standard.
Median subscription gross margin in the published survey is 81 percent against 30 percent on services. A buyer reads yours after allocating the shared costs.
Of the software, not the account
A customer who keeps the services and drops the software is churn. A buyer rebuilds retention on the software line alone.
If the services team sells the software, the buyer prices the services as a cost of sale. If the software sells the services, the services are a margin a buyer may not keep.

items.text: Hybrid models · What to fix first
Five things worth fixing before a buyer prices them.
In order of what moves the price, from the records the review reads.
Revenue and gross margin by line, by month, for the trailing 24 months, with the allocation rule written down. The split is the price.
Subscription only. Move implementation and recurring services to their own lines before a buyer does it less kindly.
On the subscription line alone, by cohort. Decide what the number is before a buyer decides it.
If the services run at a 30 percent margin, show it. A buyer who finds a 30 percent margin reported as 77 percent reopens every other number.
Owner compensation, personal expenses, one-time costs, each with the document behind it. Undocumented add-backs are removed, not argued.

sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
Should I shrink the services before going to market?
Not necessarily. Profitable services with their own margin are a position you can take. Unprofitable services bundled into software revenue are a finding. The review shows which you have.
At what services share am I priced as a services business?
Nobody publishes a threshold with data behind it. The practitioner range is 15 to 35 percent of revenue. The split, the margins and the retention on the software line decide it case by case.
Does implementation revenue count as recurring?
Not under the standard, even where every customer buys it. A buyer restates it to services.
Will the review raise my price?
We will not promise that. It shows what your numbers support and gives you the chance to fix what they do not before a buyer prices it.
